inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E pro forma net sales of standalone New Corteva (Crop Protection). 9M-2026 pro forma actual 5,357 (8-K 11-Nov-2026 EX-99.2) + Q4 estimate ~1,845. Q4-2025 pro forma was 2,173 (FY2025 pro forma 7,592 less 9M-2025 5,419); Q4 is the Latin America-heavy quarter and Q3-2026 Latin America sales fell 28% with management assuming no Brazil improvement, so Q4 is taken ~15% below prior year, consistent with guided Q4 Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA of ~157-182 against 330 in Q4-2025. FY0 is an estimate because the valuation date is 10.5 months into the fiscal year and three quarters are reported. NOT the combined-company revenue in CTVA_Metrics.csv (17,401 FY2025), which still includes Seed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ESTIMATE: 667.323M common shares outstanding at 5-Nov-2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover; unchanged by the spin, which issued no Corteva shares) plus ~3.2M for dilutive equity awards. Pre-spin the dilutive increment was 1.2M shares (9M-2026 diluted 670.7 vs basic 669.5) with a further 2.2M anti-dilutive; awards held by New Corteva employees were adjusted for the distribution, and no post-spin dilutive-securities table exists yet, so the increment is an estimate to be replaced from the FY2026 10-K. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would charge it twice. No New Corteva buyback has been announced; the flat count is a modelling convention the standalone company has not yet funded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Pro forma combined balance sheet of New Corteva at 30-Sep-2026 (8-K 11-Nov-2026, EX-99.2 page A-2), which gives effect to the 1-Oct-2026 separation: cash 1,798 + marketable securities 1; short-term borrowings 60 + long-term debt 944 (the new 6.00% 2036 notes 700, the un-exchanged stubs of the EIDP 2030/2032/2033 notes 161, medium-term notes 95, less issuance costs). The 3,078 PHI bilateral facility, the 1,100 of Vylor notes and 1,439 of exchanged EIDP notes went to Vylor. NOT the consolidated 10-Q balance sheet in CTVA_Metrics.csv (debt 7,446, cash 3,932), which is the pre-spin combined entity. 30 September is not a seasonal extreme for Crop Protection (receivables 4,106 vs 4,494 at Dec-2025 and 4,545 at Jun-2026 pro forma; customer prepayments 67 vs 346 at December), so no seasonal normalisation is applied. Q4-2026 cash flow (seasonally positive: carve-out Q4-2025 OCF was +413) is NOT credited -- FY2027 is year 1 and the Brazil receivables collection in Q4 is exactly what is in doubt; this is conservative by roughly 0.2-0.4 per share.
inputs.fcf_basis: FY2025 New Corteva carve-out combined statements (8-K 1-Oct-2026, EX-99.1): OCF from continuing operations 510 less capital expenditures 245 = 265. Less SBC incl. estimated equity-award taxes 43, less interest income 85 (stripped because net cash is added in the bridge) = 137. This carve-out figure is LEVERED on Corteva's old allocated capital structure (interest expense 175) and carries 110 of pension contributions, so it understates unlevered owner FCF; on an unlevered, pension-free basis FY2023-25 were roughly 770 / 316 / 443 before SBC (average ~510, ~36% of carve-out Operating EBITDA). It is recorded for auditability only -- the forward build is from components, not from this number.
inputs.sbc_source: New Corteva carve-out Combined Statements of Equity, FY2023-FY2025: share-based compensation 25 / 28 / 33 (an allocation from Corteva). No combined figure and no separate withholding line in the carve-out; equity-award tax withholding estimated at ~30% of SBC (the combined Corteva ratio: 23 on 78 in FY2025), giving 43.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases by the standalone entity. Pre-spin Corteva repurchased 1,071 in FY2025 and 500 in H1-2026 but that was the combined company; New Corteva's only declared return is the 0.05/share quarterly dividend (~133/yr).
inputs.fy0_note: FY2026E (estimate): 9M pro forma actuals plus guided Q4. Year 1 = FY2027.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API). Post-earnings: the print follows the 11-Nov guidance cut and the 12-Nov sell-off and sits at the 52-week low.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.2%, beta ~1.0 (pure-play crop chemicals is more cyclical than the old Seed+Crop Protection mix modelled at 0.85; FMC-type peers run 0.9-1.1), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~9.2%. The pro forma balance sheet is net cash, so debt contributes almost nothing: WACC 9.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios -- Brazil, generic pricing and standalone execution are charged in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked in the rate. This is 1.0pt above the 8.0% used for the combined company on 2026-09-26; the change is the loss of Seed's diversification, not a risk premium for the guidance cut.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside Operating EBITDA and therefore inside the flows; lease liabilities NOT added to net debt. One treatment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest (239 book, ~10/yr of income) deducted in the equity bridge at book; flows are consolidated.
inputs.pension_treatment: New Corteva, as owner of EIDP, keeps the principal U.S. pension plan and OPEB. After the ~1.5bn discretionary contribution in June/July 2026 the pro forma noncurrent liability is 789 (plus ~16 current); deducted after tax in equity_bridge. Non-operating pension cost is outside Operating EBITDA, so there is no double count.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical ag-chemicals; US filer, USD/USD). Same model family as the 2026-09-26 valuation, but a DIFFERENT ENTITY: that build valued combined Corteva (Seed + Crop Protection) at a pre-spin price; on 1-Oct-2026 Seed was distributed 1:1 as Vylor (VYLR) and CTVA is now Crop Protection only. Every driver was rebuilt from standalone sources; nothing was carried over except the method, the tax-calibration approach and the hurdle. SOURCES: CTVA_Metrics.csv and SEC XBRL for CIK 1755672 still carry the COMBINED history (and Vylor is the accounting successor), so the base is New Corteva's own carve-out and pro forma statements filed on Form 8-K: 1-Oct-2026 (audited carve-out FY2023-25, pro forma FY2025 and H1-2026), 11-Nov-2026 (Q3 release, 30-Sep-2026 pro forma balance sheet and 9M pro forma P&L) and 12-Nov-2026 (9M carve-out). These are not in research/CTVA/Extracted and were read from EDGAR. TWO BASES, do not mix: carve-out (FY2025 sales 7,840, Operating EBITDA 1,486) and pro forma (sales 7,592, Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA 1,267); the ~220 gap is the Vylor commercial agreements (-189) and standalone cost (-31). Guidance and this model are on the PRO FORMA basis. EBITDA PATH = Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA margin less ~2.0pp of recurring cash leakage that the adjusted metric excludes: (1) restructuring and litigation 'significant items' recur every year (486 / 251 / 8 in FY2023-25, 250 in 9M-2026, a further 130-140 programme to 2028) -- ~1.0-1.2pp in cash; (2) exchange losses, the cost of hedging BRL and other soft currencies, 299 / 170 / 76 / 46 (9M-26) -- ~0.8pp. Leakage falls to 1.5pp after the manufacturing restructuring completes in 2028. FY2026E anchor: guided EBITDA 1,100-1,125 on ~7,200 = 15.4% operating. CASH TAX 30% of EBIT: carve-out current tax (provision less deferred) averaged ~300 on ~1,000 of operating EBIT in FY2023-25; ~80/yr of DowDuPont-era amortization is non-deductible and Brazil losses are not fully benefited. The 9M-2026 pro forma base rate of 15% is not treated as repeatable (9M-2025: 31.8%). D&A 5.8% -> 4.5% as that amortization runs off (intangibles 978); capex 3.4-3.6% (245 on 7,592 in FY2025). WORKING CAPITAL: receivables 4,106 + inventory 2,661 less payables 2,514 = ~59% of sales, the Latin American credit book; wc_capture -40% of incremental revenue. CHECK: base year-1 owner FCF ~490 (6.7% of sales) against ~350-450 implied by FY2023-25 history on the pro forma basis -- the build is at the top of that range because it assumes receivables stop growing faster than sales; see key risks. BEAR year-1 margin is set 0.5pp lower than the story alone implies, to offset the engine crediting a working-capital release on the revenue decline that a Brazil destock would not deliver.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the cut guide; Brazil stops falling in 2027 on easier comparisons but mature-molecule pricing does not recover. New actives and biologicals carry 3-3.5% growth and restructuring savings lift the operating margin back to ~18% by 2031.

bear.margin_note: Operating margin 13.5 / 13.5 / 14.0 / 14.3 / 14.5 thereafter, less leakage 2.0pp throughout (restructuring never ends); year 1 a further 0.5pp lower to offset the engine's working-capital release on falling revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: New Corteva delivers the cut FY2026 guide (Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA ~1.11bn on ~7.2bn of sales, a 15.4% margin against 16.7% in FY2025). In 2027 Brazilian channel inventory clears and comparisons ease, but pricing on off-patent herbicides and fungicides stays where Chinese, Indian and UPL generics have pushed it and U.S. acetochlor does not come back. Growth of 3-3.5% comes from the patent-protected actives (Arylex, Zorvec, Enlist-system herbicides), biologicals rebuilding toward their target, and the seed-applied technology supply to Vylor. The 2026 workforce actions (115-125 of run-rate savings company-wide) and the manufacturing network programme take the operating margin back to ~18% by 2031 -- the FY2022-23 level, not better. Significant items and hedging losses keep absorbing ~2pp of sales in cash until the restructuring finishes in 2028, and the Latin American receivables book consumes 40 cents of every incremental sales dollar.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Brazil collapse proves to be a liquidity-driven destock rather than a structural share loss: farmer credit eases as rates fall, the channel restocks in 2027-28, and revenue grows 5-6% for three years. New-product mix outruns generic erosion, biologicals reach ~1bn of sales, and the pure-play cost base (one function set, a rationalised plant network) lifts the operating margin to ~19.5% -- about where the segment peaked in FY2022, now on a leaner structure. Working capital intensity eases slightly as Brazilian terms normalise. It needs Brazil, pricing and execution to go right together.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Q3-2026 shortfall is the start of a structural reset rather than a trough: generic pricing pressure spreads from Brazil and U.S. acetochlor to more of the mature portfolio, distributors keep buying just-in-time, and a weak farm-income cycle (low corn and soy prices, high Brazilian rates) holds volumes down. Sales fall again in 2027 and then grow ~2% nominal. Without Seed's royalties to cushion it, the operating margin settles at 14-14.5% -- below any year in the segment's history -- and restructuring becomes permanent, so cash leakage never falls. Receivables stretch further. Legacy PFAS and product-liability costs beyond the accrual (576 of disclosed potential exposure) are a further tail not in the flows; the bear case stays above the zero-TV floor and the net-cash balance sheet means this is an earnings bear, not a solvency one.
scenario_narratives.separation_note: The 1-Oct-2026 spin moved the Seed business and ~5.6bn of debt to Vylor; holders of record on 24-Sep received one VYLR per CTVA. This DCF values CTVA as it trades now, Crop Protection only. It is not comparable with the 2026-09-26 valuation of the combined company without adding the separately valued VYLR -- see reconciliation.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (house default 15%): guidance was cut by ~15% within six weeks of the company becoming standalone, which says management's visibility into the Brazilian channel is poor, and the pressure on mature molecules is from structural generic capacity, not a single bad season. It is not higher because the balance sheet is net cash with no refinancing risk, so the downside is margin, not solvency. Base 50%: the cut guide embeds no Brazil recovery in Q4 and the FY2027 assumptions only require the decline to stop. Bull 20% (default 35%): it needs a Brazilian credit recovery, a pricing floor and standalone execution together, on a four-year record of zero net sales growth.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on standalone New Corteva -- the Crop Protection business that kept the CTVA ticker after Seed was spun off as Vylor on 1-Oct-2026. The model is built on the company's own pro forma basis (which is what guidance is given on) rather than on the richer carve-out or segment figures, and takes a further ~2pp of sales off the adjusted EBITDA margin for the restructuring, litigation and currency-hedging costs that recur every year but are excluded from 'operating' results. The balance sheet is the 30-Sep-2026 pro forma: net cash of ~0.8bn, more than offset by ~1.3bn of pension, legacy environmental, litigation, tax-matters and minority claims that stay with this entity. Value rests on whether a 15-16% margin is a trough or the new level: the base case assumes a partial recovery to the FY2022-23 level by 2031, capitalised at a 14x cap that binds.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash conversion: on FY2023-25 carve-out history roughly 36% of Operating EBITDA reached unlevered free cash flow before SBC. The base case's year-1 owner FCF (~490) is at the top of what that history supports, because it assumes receivables stop growing faster than sales. If Brazilian credit terms keep stretching, value is lower than modelled in every scenario.

Brazil and mature-molecule pricing: Q3-2026 Latin America organic sales fell 31% and management assumes no improvement in 2026. Whether this is a destock (base, bull) or a structural reset (bear) is the single largest driver; each 1pp of steady-state EBITDA margin is worth roughly 0.9 per share in the base case.

Standalone basis is thin: one quarter of pro forma results, no standalone 10-K, a fully diluted share count that is estimated, and carve-out tax and cost allocations that will be restated. FY2026E revenue is itself an estimate (Q4 not reported).

Legacy liabilities: New Corteva keeps EIDP's stray liabilities -- PFAS (Chemours MOU), environmental sites, the principal U.S. pension plan. Only accrued amounts are deducted; disclosed potential exposure above the environmental accrual is a further 576 (~0.85 per share pre-tax).
Terminal value: the cap multiple binds in all three scenarios (14x base against a ~16x Gordon value), so the result is sensitive to the multiple chosen for a cyclical, low-growth chemical business.

Cash tax: 30% of EBIT is calibrated to three carve-out years on a separate-return basis; the 9M-2026 pro forma base rate was 15%. A sustainably lower standalone rate would add value; it is not assumed.
